phase: V4b under review; THE GAUNTLET IS RUNNING
phaseNote: The gauntlet has a blind A/B in flight on GUNFEEL for the first time — headed, prod build, 1440x900, in an isolated git worktree so its builders cannot collide with V4. Setting it up found two apparatus defects: a blanket node_modules symlink resolved @doomcraft/shared back to the MAIN tree (the worktree would have compiled against the wrong source), and capture-ours reuses whatever already holds its port, so a capture could silently photograph the other tree. Both closed. V4b went to Codex as 16 numbered clauses and was REFUSED: 12 correct, 4 broken. Every finding reproduced here in both directions. It found a LIVE defect in shipped code — items kind/rarity lookups admit Object.prototype members, so kind:"constructor" parses clean, ItemDef.kind becomes a FUNCTION, and kind:"constructor" and kind:"toString" emit the identical fingerprint line: two different manifests, one digest. Same bug 8c6f196 fixed in variants, never fixed in items.

log.m: Bar confirmed reachable — headed Chrome defeats the Cloudflare interstitial.
Captured voxiom.io live: menu, in-game HUD, 60.2 fps median, 3.16 s to interactive.
Wrote ref/BAR.md — seven measured weaknesses in the bar become the product strategy.
Spine workflow launched: contract -> renderer / world / server in parallel -> integration gate.
Mobile bar captured. voxiom REFUSES to play in portrait — 'Please rotate your screen'. Landscape has no fire button; aim and shoot are the same gesture.
Re-measured the bar under 4x CPU throttle (throttle verified linear): 60.2 median but 1% low falls to 53.8. Beating the bar = >53.8; our spec of 55 is deliberately harder.
Spine RUNS. 25,330 lines, 18/18 + 19/19 + 29/29 tests green. Real voxel world, HUD, 7 Doom weapons, 6 players, 33 entities, zero console errors.
Perf measured honestly: headed + throttled we are 60.2/53.8 — IDENTICAL to the bar. The 120 fps was a headless capture artifact. A tie is a loss.
Scope expanded by user: quest mode, builder mode, multiplayer, more modes. Captured DOOM 1993 (E1M1, real gameplay) and verified Minecraft Classic as two new bars.
Spine final: dynamic crosshair spread, 7-pellet shotgun sparks, killfeed, in-engine menu, full settings panel, 3 reserved ad slots. 312 ms to interactive, zero console errors.
Mobile PORTRAIT confirmed playable by eye — big FIRE pad, labelled JUMP/CRCH/RUN/RLD/BLD, real joystick. The bar refuses portrait entirely. Decisive win.
Mode framework landed (level format = data, 3 Quest levels). Four mode builders still in flight at pause.
Queued by user: advertiser-buyable in-game ads, GTA mode, ElevenLabs voices. GTA bar NOT yet obtainable — flagged, not faked. Paused for handover; resume 22:00.

Economy layer specced (docs/ECONOMY.md): 2 currencies, tradable cosmetics, escrow trading, viral sharing, competitions. Three architecture calls: server grants all rewards; no loot boxes / no real-money tradables by default; sponsor PLATFORM is buildable, a sponsor deal is not mine to make.
Sponsor spec done. Key finding: the 1.5% screen-coverage floor (not fog) is the binding constraint on in-world ads — a 4x2 m billboard only qualifies within 7.7 m, so author at 16x8 m minimum.

Rejected client-side WebGL2 occlusion queries: 0.19 ms spike lands on the 18.6 ms p99 tail = 53.2 fps 1% low, under our 53.8 line. Chose server-side reconstruction from existing yaw/pitch inputs — 0.000 ms client cost.
TWO REAL BUGS found, unrelated to ads: net pump runs inside rAF so backgrounding the tab 15 s DISCONNECTS you mid-match; and there is no CSP anywhere on the server. See docs/BUGS-FOUND.md.

User decisions: run BOTH programmatic (AdSense/networks) as fill AND direct-sold as it arrives; support ALL THREE prize shapes. Flagged: AdSense covers page slots only — in-game/rewarded needs a games network (the bar uses AdInPlay).
Textures landed and measured: dark surfaces 0.66->2.72 and 0.84->3.39 grey levels, inside the bar band. At matched luminance our sand 3.62 vs bar 3.32, grass 4.35 vs 4.39 — dead level.
Found the metric is scale-dependent: voxiom own sand reads 1.80 at nose, 3.32 mid, 8.51 far. The "3.32 band" was one slice of a curve. Our depth curve now sits on theirs.
Both real bugs fixed: net pump off rAF (tab-background no longer disconnects), CSP added. Regression to fix: quest tile floor went 4.03 -> 2.56 because seam strength was cut.
Handover plan written: Phase A economy, B sponsors/ads, C platform, D defects. GitHub push blocked until tools/.profile-mc (Cookies + Login Data) is purged from 2 commits of history.
A1 reward spine: EntitlementGuard + trust.ts (1,766 lines) were imported by nothing. Now on every live match. 1503 → 1562 tests.

Audit found a proven __proto__ self-grant past guardProfileWrite (1e9 XP), Math.random() account secrets, an unauthenticated account-link, a join-code leak. All closed; exploits re-run against the real binary.
Two decision docs: docs/PACKS.md (content packs; CONTENT_VERSION gates nothing today) and docs/PLATFORM.md (accounts, console, profile).
Server tier LIVE on Railway: doomcraft-production.up.railway.app — document + rooms from one origin; /api/version folds level hashes; /api/levels mounted; admin console at /admin behind the bearer.
Admin console at /admin on the Node origin; flags (runtime registry, freeze, force/rollout with typed confirm), fleet, entitlement ring, journal, player lookup. applyServerFlags finally has a caller.

Accounts: scrypt passphrases, sessions, FIRST SIGNUP BECOMES THE OWNER (proven: two owners without the lock, one with). Audit found and we closed: player-cookie throttle bypass, CSRF owner-claim via text/plain form, unreadable accounts file re-opening bootstrap.
Landing site live: doomcraft-site.vercel.app — Play now → Railway, Play offline → Vercel static.
Session start. Baseline captured to a file: 105 files / 2525 tests + 3 skips green in 78 s; release:verify PASS, 16 checks. Tree clean at d0d246a.
Stage 1 plan written as seven numbered clauses and put to Codex read-only BEFORE any code — the standing rule that has overturned a central design clause four sessions running.

CODEX VERDICT. C1/C2/C4 stand. C3 was WRONG: a NaN radius does not enter carveSphere’s loop, and a radius clamp does not make it terminate — centre 1e20 radius 1 still hangs, because y0===y1 and y++ cannot advance. C5 was INCOMPLETE: eleven more simulation fields (kind, ammo, projectileGravity/Radius/LifeMs, spinDownMs, switchInMs/OutMs, recoilPitch/Yaw/Recovery) are invisible to the proposed ratchet. C6 was VACUOUS — it reproduced a green-with-revert. C7, the stage’s own claim, is false as written.

THREE NEW DEFECTS, all confirmed here by reading the source. (1) packs.declared never checks the declared INPUTS — lying inputs with a correct fingerprint pass BOTH gates, and the inputs are the only reason the ratchet prints a line diff instead of two hex numbers. (2) The offline gate has no MAX_PACK_INPUT_BYTES check; only the service gate does. (3) decodeVariantTable reads 16 f64 values with no finite/integer/band check, so the wire accepts a NaN damage and a magSize of 7.5 that the parser refuses.

PELLET CEILING SHIPPED. MAX_PELLETS moved to shared; the server now clamps AND reads hot.pellets. Two tests, and each half of the fix has its own: at 20 pellets the u8 does not wrap so only the CEILING shows (revert → expected 20 to be 16); at 260 it wraps to 4 so only the SOURCE shows (revert → expected 16 to be 4). The original line fails both. Lockstep golden and the cone agreement did not move — 72 tests green.

HORDE SHOP TEST SHIPPED. The obvious version was vacuous: Horde starts owning the shotgun, so buying one takes the quarter-price ammo branch and horde.ts:2054 never runs — green with the fix reverted on all four observables. The real test buys an UNOWNED chaingun against a magSize-50 variant. Revert → expected 100 to be 50, and the equipStart test stays green under the same revert, so the two lines are separately covered.

CARVESPHERE BOUNDED, both implementations. The radius clamp was never the fix — a centre of 1e20 with a radius of ONE lands y0===y1 and hangs identically, so the three loop RANGES are clamped to the world box and the if (y<1||y>=CHUNK_HEIGHT) continue is deleted: a continue inside a loop whose counter cannot advance just spins faster. Two findings beyond the brief: Infinity is a fourth hang mode the plan never named (floor(Infinity) is Infinity, and it passes radius<=0), and a non-finite POWER in the client carve removes 72 voxels against a rocket real 36 — it carves through obsidian, because NaN <= resistance is false so the survived branch never runs. In-range carves unchanged block for block: 53 removals and digest 78d994cb before and after.

THE VARIANT WIRE NOW REFUSES WHAT THE PARSER REFUSES. decodeVariantTable read 16 f64s with no checks; it accepted a NaN damage (NaN at every range), a magSize of 7.5 (hot.magSize narrows to 7 — a magazine filled to a full magazine is not full), and — the case the plan missed — a magSize of -7, which narrows to 65529. All five refused now, and a legitimate table still decodes. The builder stopped on something better than the fix: the FROZEN golden vector is a row no parser could ever emit — it declares base 1 (shotgun) and carries the pistol rpm 420 against the shotgun band of 22.5..120 — so as long as that literal stands, this door can never be band-checked. It refused to edit the frozen literal and wrote the constraint down as a test instead.

THE GATE NOW CHECKS ITS OWN DECLARED INPUT LINES. checkPacksDeclared compared the fingerprint and read the checked-in input literals ONLY to render a failure diff — so inputs of ["0:lies"] with a correct fingerprint passed both gates. The literals exist precisely so a firing ratchet prints a field-level LINE DIFF instead of two hex numbers, which means the reviewable artifact could be a lie. Also: the offline gate had no MAX_PACK_INPUT_BYTES check at all — a 161-byte line passed release:verify and was caught only by the service gate. Both now go through one shared helper. release:verify is 17 checks.

THE CRITIC BROKE MY OWN TEST. It decoupled the client pellet loop from report.pellets and all 15 tests stayed green while the client resolved 260 pellets against the server 4 — because report.pellets is a scalar that TRAVELS WITH the behaviour. Rewritten to count the hits the client loop actually registered against a real target; the attack now fails at expected 20 to be 16 and expected 260 to be 4. It also falsified two comment claims of mine, both now corrected: a re-export justified by callers that do not exist, and a stale argument for the integer rail that this very change had invalidated.

THE WEAPONS RATCHET IS 38 FIELDS, weapons@2, 0xbfdd37e6. It watched 13 while both predictors read 38 — Codex named 11 the plan had missed, including switch timing, which GATES SHOTS (a shotgun switchInMs of 300 vs 600 moves first-fire eligibility from 440 ms to 740 ms) and recoil, which moves the camera that supplies the firing direction. reserveMax is deleted rather than widened: its only reader in the repo was this fingerprint, and reserve is per AMMO TYPE, so it was not merely unread but the wrong shape. Every one of the 38 fields now has its own sensitivity test — drop spreadAir from the line and four tests go red. Longest line 140 bytes against the 160 cap.

FULL SUITE: 2592 passed, 3 skipped. Five failures, all in synth.test.ts and chunkz.test.ts — the two load-sensitive flakes the handover names. Evidence they are load and not regression: neither file is touched by this stage, the run took 366s against a 78s baseline because another project was running its own suite on this machine throughout, and both pass 51/51 in isolation immediately afterwards. Recorded in .verify/runs/ rather than dismissed — they remain undiagnosed wall-clock assertions with no headroom, and making them robust is a piece of work, not a footnote.

STAGE 1 COMMITTED (9f3b472). Also fixed a doc comment that claimed sandbox and the tutorial call Room.grantAllWeapons — grep finds no caller of that METHOD outside tests; the sandbox hits are plan.grantAllWeapons, a different mechanism. The builder checked my framing instead of inheriting it, which is the third false claim caught in prose today.

CODEX ON V4: "I would not approve V4 as written." Nine of eleven clauses broken. It also found a REGRESSION in the stage I had committed an hour earlier: the parser tolerates EPS=1e-9 on a band floor and the negative rail I added to the decoder that morning refuses exactly, so a manifest with spreadPerShot -1e-10 parses clean, gates GREEN, and leaves a real Room with 0 variant rows. A published pack serving nothing, with no error anywhere. Reproduced all four measurements here before believing it.

THE TWO DOORS NOW AGREE BY CONSTRUCTION. Not by adding the same check twice — the three archetype-free rules run as a contiguous PREFIX in the decoder order, because two lists agree by construction only when one is literally the prefix of the other. The invariant sweep is 7616 probes; on the old code it named 108 manifests the parser blessed and the wire refused. Two corrections to my brief: "a value must survive its own narrowing" is FALSE for the f32 fields (f32(4.4) is 4.400000095367432 and arsenal.ts documents six such lossy pairs as shipped behaviour, so equality would refuse the compiled table itself), and rpm:-0 slips past every negative check because -0 < 0 is false. Also moved the Room end-to-end test out of shared/ — it was pulling eleven server modules into shared's build.

TWO MORE SHIPPED DEFECTS CLOSED. damageEntity wrote the weapon the killer was HOLDING at the moment of death rather than the one that fired — rocket in flight, switch to chainsaw, demon dies, feed says chainsaw. The builder found a second instance my brief had explicitly ruled out: melee is wrong SYNCHRONOUSLY, because a punch fires as tryFire(p, CHAINSAW) while you hold something else. And an invalid NEWEST data pack vanished before the gate could refuse it: installedPacks omits a kind whose newest version fails to parse, so a broken variants@2 made the gate return ok with no variants row at all, silently losing the good v1 too. Campaign, items and quests shared the hole; levels structurally did not.

ROUND TWO COMMITTED (d3528a1). Full suite genuinely green this time: 107 files, 2622 passed, 3 skipped, ZERO failures in 96.88s — which retroactively confirms the five earlier failures were the machine and not the code. The last builder found a hazard my own brief created: putting a display name into the fingerprint line means a name carrying a newline makes a one-variant manifest hash as a two-variant one, because the digest is inputs.join(newline). It closed the original hole without opening that one. Five of six briefs I wrote today contained a claim the builder correctly overturned — the line telling agents to report anything wrong in the brief is now the highest-yield sentence in the template.

DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED. Railway SUCCESS; the origin reports weapons@2 — a pack version that exists only in this commit, which is stronger proof than build.id (which lies) or a bundle hash. Live smoke gate 14/14, including the two checks that are the only thing anywhere able to catch a deployed room factory that forgot its pinned content. TWO CORRECTIONS: the weapons@2 deploy hazard I called blocking all session did NOT apply — the live release is revision 0, the compiled-in builtin, so no stored release existed to orphan, and one curl would have settled it hours earlier. And the handover Vercel bundle-hash rule CANNOT PASS from this machine: I reproduced the build id correctly (it is in the served bundle) but Rollup hashes our own chunks differently on Linux than on arm64 macOS while the vendor chunk stays byte-identical. Replaced with a check that names the commit directly.

THREE VERIFICATION METHODS MEASURED THE WRONG THING TODAY: a pellet test asserting a scalar set beside the loop rather than by it; ls | head -1 picking a bundle alphabetically instead of newest; and a bundle-hash rule that cannot reproduce across build platforms. Same shape each time — the instrument was never checked against a known answer. That is HANDOVER rule 28 turning out to have three more instances than the day it was written.

V4 SPLIT INTO FIVE SUB-PHASES, recorded in docs/VARIANTS.md §5a. The conclusion from the refusal was not just its nine findings but its verdict on SHAPE: a phase whose plan can be broken in nine places is a phase too big to judge. V4a is the smallest piece that puts real content through the whole V1-V3 machine end to end — and it is buildable only now, because variantsFileFor deliberately had no content/ fallback until the variants-aware binary was live, which it is as of this afternoon deploy.

THE GAUNTLET HARNESS STILL WORKS. tools/capture-ours.mjs produced 86 frames, the twelve baseline points lining up 1:1 with ref/voxiom/desktop-*.png — our last capture was Aug 22, before the economy, sponsors and variants work. Looked at the combat frame rather than the exit code: real render, textured blocks, a detailed rocket-launcher viewmodel, corner-only HUD, visible light shafts against the bar flat lighting. Real GPU too (ANGLE Metal, M3 Pro), not SwiftShader. BUT THE NUMBERS ARE NOT COMPARABLE YET: 120.5 fps median is headless and unthrottled — the handover already records that the 120 fps was a headless capture artifact and that headed plus 4x throttle put us at 60.2/53.8, IDENTICAL to the bar. And 8.85 MB transfer is the dev server unminified, not the 3.34 MB prod figure. A fair A/B needs --headed --prod and the same throttle on both sides.

V4a IS LIVE. content/variants.json ships two rows — a slug shotgun trading seven 11-damage pellets for one 62-damage slug and paying in rate (budget +2.0%), and a swift rocket buying speed and rate with damage and blast (budget -1.21%). Two entries, not four: a variant has ONE base, so covering hitscan and projectile takes two and a third would exist only to make the table look fuller. The content/ fallback finally exists because its blocking condition — the variants-aware binary being live — was met by this afternoon deploy, and packsRoot wins so a bundled definition can never replace an installed one.

AND THE DEPLOY GATE CAN FINALLY FAIL. tools/smoke-signal.mjs is called in the handover the only check that can see a deployed binary whose room factory forgot its pinned content. Its predicate was d[0] === 13 — a lone opcode byte satisfied it, an empty table satisfied it, it proved a message was SENT. Sixth gate this session found reporting green while testing nothing. It now asks /api/version which version the origin pins and asserts pinned means non-empty in BOTH directions. Production: variants@1 pinned, 2 rows on the wire, named. An hour ago the same line would have printed ok for one byte.

stages.name: V1-V3 closeout
stages.what: Five verified loose ends: the server pellet clamp, carveSphere's unbounded loop, the dead reserveMax field, the weapons ratchet that covers 13 fields while the predictors read 28, and the horde SHOP delivery line with no test.
stages.detail: Committed 9f3b472 + 1d0dfb4. Nine pieces, every one proven red with itself reverted. Three defects came from Codex attacking the plan before a line was written, three more from critics attacking the finished work — one of them in my own test.

stages.name: V4 — now five sub-phases
stages.what: Split after the review refused it as one phase. V4a: the pack reaches a room (content/variants.json, the content/ fallback, the gate emitting kind 7) — no ownership, every player still at slot 0. V4b: the ownership token. V4c: the claim reaches the body. V4d: display truth — the killfeed cannot tell two shotgun variants apart. V4e: acquisition, which as specified leaves variant supply at zero forever.
stages.detail: V4a DONE and deployed (ef1100d). V4b-V4e specified in docs/VARIANTS.md §5a with the trap each one carries. Nobody can own or equip a variant yet — every player still resolves to slot 0.

stages.name: Achievements
stages.what: New scope. Server grants every reward; a banked-but-unpayable achievement needs a DEBT not a counter; the condition must be expressible in pack SCHEMA, never shipped code; mode availability is a column on the trust table, never an if.

stages.name: The gauntlet — 0/23
stages.what: 23 pieces, each judged blind against the real captured frames in ref/. GUNFEEL is in flight now — builder, capture steward and a blind critic, up to 4 rounds. Fair-A/B rules enforced: headed + prod build, matched viewport, and the neutral metrics files the critic reads (a default headless dev run reports ~120 fps median, an uncapped-vsync artifact this project was fooled by once).

stages.name: The rest of the queue
stages.what: V5's standing gate, portals/TWA, C7 analytics, the deathmatch share surface, and the two sponsor loose ends.
